sheet-19-1.description: The main part of sheet 19 covers the south-western corner of the Sea Girt grid in 1905, drawn at 120 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It runs from Park Avenue at the top to Mott Avenue and Sea Girt Avenue in the lower right, and from 3rd Avenue at the right edge west across 4th and 5th Avenues to the double-track New York and Long Branch Railroad and the short end of 6th Avenue beyond it. East of 5th Avenue the blocks between Park, Newell, Stockton, Central, Hamilton and Mott Avenues are platted into narrow numbered lots and are almost entirely empty. Between 5th Avenue and the railroad lies the Sea Girt Farm and Water Works, with a greenhouse range, storage and hose house, tanks and pumping plant on block 89, its blocks 88 and 89 drawn with dashed lot lines. West of the tracks are a freight house, the depot platform, a post office and a few dwellings on Stockton Avenue, and the Pennsylvania Railroad branch curves in at the lower left. The lower half of the part is the open ground of the New Jersey Military Encampment, bounded by Sea Girt Avenue running diagonally south-east and Encampment Avenue running south beside the railroad; it shows the Governor's headquarters, a mess building, the commissary along the track and a compass rose. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths of 60 and 80 feet are marked. The encampment buildings themselves are drawn in a separate inset below the heavy line (part 2), which is not part of this annotation.
notes: Old names and modern OpenStreetMap names: Park Avenue is Philadelphia Boulevard, Newell Avenue is Boston Boulevard, Stockton Avenue is Crescent Parkway (east of the railroad), Central Avenue is Washington Boulevard, Hamilton Avenue is Trenton Boulevard, Mott Avenue is Stockton Boulevard, Encampment Avenue is Camp Drive.
Crescent Parkway (old Stockton Avenue) lies about 7 m north of the drawn centreline today; it was left out of the control.
The 1905 6th Avenue west of the railroad does not line up with modern 6th or 7th Avenue; modern 6th Avenue runs along the east side of the tracks.
Sea Girt Farm and Water Works on block 89; Governor's headquarters (lettered 'Govenor's Head Quarters') on the encampment ground.
The north arrow is about 9 degrees anticlockwise of true north (magnetic north).

Map, 120 ft to an inch, north toward upper left (arrow magnetic, about 9 deg west of true). Two parts: part 1 main map (Park to Mott Av, 3rd Av west to the railroad and 6th Av; Sea Girt Farm and Water Works; New Jersey Military Encampment ground); part 2 inset below the heavy line: New Jersey Military Encampment Buildings on Encampment Av, drawn at a different rotation, no street junction, not placed. Old Park/Newell/Stockton/Central/Hamilton/Mott Av = Philadelphia/Boston Blvd, Crescent Pkwy, Washington/Trenton/Stockton Blvd; Encampment Av = Camp Drive.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: New Jersey Military Encampment Buildings (mess hall, store house, Encampment Avenue) (no street junction; drawn at a different rotation from the main map (inset arrow about 41 deg clockwise of the main one); modern Camp Drive ends short of the drawn buildings; needs hand-picked control from buildings or parcel corners of the National Guard Training Center, if any survive).

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers the south-eastern part of Sea Girt in 1905, at 120 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It runs from Park Avenue at the top to Franklin Avenue and Sea Girt Avenue at the bottom, and from 3rd Avenue at the left edge east across 2nd and 1st Avenues to Ocean Avenue and the beach of the Atlantic Ocean. The western half is a regular grid of narrow numbered lots between Park, Newell, Stockton, Central, Hamilton, Mott, Salem and Franklin Avenues, nearly all vacant. The centre of the sheet is Crescent Park, an oval landscaped ground with dashed walks, bounded on the west by the curve of Crescent Avenue from Park Avenue down to Hamilton Avenue. East of the park, block 7 along Ocean Avenue holds a row of large dwellings on deep lots. Below Hamilton Avenue the Beach House hotel fills the block between 1st and Ocean Avenues, with its kitchen, servants' buildings, ice house, tool house, gasoline machine, bath houses and a note that a watchman is kept during the closed season and there is no fire apparatus. Further south are small blocks along Salem and Franklin Avenues, a fish house near Ocean Avenue, and the triangular blocks cut by Sea Girt Avenue running diagonally to the south-west corner. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along 1st Avenue and the park, and street widths of 60, 80 and 100 feet are given.
notes: Old names and modern OpenStreetMap names: Park Avenue is Philadelphia Boulevard, Newell Avenue is Boston Boulevard, Stockton Avenue is Crescent Parkway, Central Avenue is Washington Boulevard, Hamilton Avenue is Trenton Boulevard, Mott Avenue is Stockton Boulevard, Salem Avenue is Neptune Place, Franklin Avenue is Seaside Place, Crescent Avenue is The Crescent.
Modern 1st Avenue continues north through the former Crescent Park; in 1905 1st Avenue began at Hamilton Avenue.
Ocean Avenue south of Hamilton Avenue no longer follows the drawn line.
Beach House hotel between 1st Avenue and Ocean Avenue.

Map, 120 ft to an inch. Park Av to Franklin Av, 3rd Av to Ocean Av: Crescent Park, Beach House hotel. Salem Av = Neptune Place, Franklin Av = Seaside Place, Crescent Av = The Crescent. Faint ink: detector ink_below_paper auto (80).

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers the north-western part of Sea Girt in 1905, at 120 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It runs from Wreck Pond and Terrace Avenue at the top to Park Avenue at the bottom, and from 3rd Avenue at the right edge west across 4th and 5th Avenues, the double-track New York and Long Branch Railroad and 6th Avenue to the left edge. The streets between Terrace and Park Avenues are Bellevue, Clinton, Sherwood, Fairmount and Olden Avenues, all 80 feet wide. Every block is platted into narrow numbered lots, and the sheet is almost entirely vacant: one dwelling on block 68 near Terrace Avenue, two small buildings on block 62 and a tool house beside the railroad on block 100 are all that is drawn. The blocks west of the railroad are cut at an angle to follow the tracks and 6th Avenue, and the land north of Bellevue Avenue west of the railroad is open ground along the shore of Wreck Pond, where a compass rose is drawn. The railroad crosses Wreck Pond on a bridge at the top of the sheet. Lot dimensions of 50 and 60 feet and street widths are marked; there are no water pipes on this sheet.
notes: Old names and modern OpenStreetMap names: Terrace Avenue is The Terrace, Bellevue Avenue is Beacon Boulevard, Clinton Avenue is Chicago Boulevard, Sherwood Avenue is Brooklyn Boulevard, Fairmount Avenue is New York Boulevard, Olden Avenue is Baltimore Boulevard, Park Avenue is Philadelphia Boulevard.
The 1905 6th Avenue west of the railroad lies 15 to 20 m from modern 7th Avenue and was not used for control; modern 6th Avenue runs along the east side of the tracks, through the drawn lots.
The rail crossing of Beacon Boulevard was rejected (7.5 m from the street fit).

Map, 120 ft to an inch. Wreck Pond/Terrace Av to Park Av, 3rd Av west across the New York and Long Branch RR to 6th Av; nearly vacant. Terrace/Bellevue/Clinton/Sherwood/Fairmount/Olden Av = The Terrace, Beacon/Chicago/Brooklyn/New York/Baltimore Blvd. Old 6th Av west of the railroad is displaced against modern 7th Av; left out.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 covers the north-eastern part of Sea Girt in 1905, at 120 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It runs from Wreck Pond and Terrace Avenue at the top to Park Avenue at the bottom, and from 3rd Avenue at the left edge east across 2nd and 1st Avenues to Ocean Avenue and the beach of the Atlantic Ocean. Bellevue, Clinton, Sherwood, Fairmount and Olden Avenues cross the sheet between Terrace and Park Avenues. A road leads north from Terrace Avenue to a bridge over Wreck Pond, lettered as the bridge to Spring Lake. Most of the building is in the north-east: the United States lighthouse with its oil house at Ocean Avenue between Terrace and Bellevue Avenues, a row of dwellings on block 1 beside it, the Parker House and the Tremont House hotel on block 2 between Bellevue and Clinton Avenues, and scattered dwellings on blocks 32, 33 and 34 along 1st Avenue. Further west and south the blocks are platted into narrow numbered lots and largely vacant, apart from a few dwellings and the Church of St. Uriel at the corner of 3rd and Park Avenues. The blocks east of 1st Avenue are divided into deeper lots facing Ocean Avenue. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along Bellevue Avenue and 1st Avenue; street widths of 60, 80 and 100 feet are given. A compass rose is drawn on the beach.
notes: Old names and modern OpenStreetMap names: Terrace Avenue is The Terrace, Bellevue Avenue is Beacon Boulevard, Clinton Avenue is Chicago Boulevard, Sherwood Avenue is Brooklyn Boulevard, Fairmount Avenue is New York Boulevard, Olden Avenue is Baltimore Boulevard, Park Avenue is Philadelphia Boulevard.
U.S. Light House (Sea Girt Lighthouse) at Ocean Avenue and Bellevue Avenue (today Beacon Boulevard).
Tremont House and Parker House hotels on block 2; Church of St. Uriel at 3rd Avenue and Park Avenue.
Map, 120 ft to an inch. Wreck Pond/Terrace Av to Park Av, 3rd Av to Ocean Av: U.S. Light House, Tremont House, Parker House, Church of St. Uriel. Pilot sheet.
